scenario.briefing: The port parser needs tests for a valid value, a zero boundary, and malformed text before the rover console ships.

accessibility.summary: The Zig workspace is keyboard accessible. Checks verify source structure; they do not compile or run Zig.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between the editor and results. Ctrl+Enter runs the checks.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each check announces its description, whether it passed, and the missing or forbidden source fragment.

title: Assertions that fail for the right reason
summary: Write value and error assertions with std.testing, then repair a test that swallows every failure.

objectives.description: Write value and error assertions in test blocks.
Find a test that ignores the error it should assert.
Predict how a failed expectEqual ends a test.

hints: Test blocks live beside the code they cover.
expectEqual compares a known value with the parser result.
expectError requires the exact expected error.
Unwrap a successful parse with try before comparing.

misconceptions.description: Catching and discarding the error inside a test.
misconceptions.feedback: An empty catch makes the test pass whether the parser succeeds or fails. Assert the error explicitly with expectError.

misconceptions.description: Leaving a test block without assertions.
misconceptions.testDescription: The valid-port test compares the parsed value.
misconceptions.feedback: A test with no failing assertion proves nothing. Call expectEqual or expectError and unwrap successes with try.

misconceptions.description: Believing a failed expectation only prints a message.
misconceptions.feedback: std.testing.expectEqual returns an error on mismatch. In a test, returning that error marks the test as failed.

misconceptions.description: Accepting any error instead of the exact case.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Calling expectError(anyerror, ...) so a wrong failure still passes the boundary test.
misconceptions.feedback: Assert the specific expected error. anyerror hides a parser that returns the wrong failure for the right input.

sections.title: Tests live beside the code
sections.body: A Zig test block is declared with test "name" { ... } and compiled only for test builds. Put boundary tests in the same file as the parser so they can call private functions. zig test src/main.zig runs them directly; zig build test runs the named step from the build graph.

sections.title: Assert values and errors
sections.body: std.testing.expectEqual(expected, actual) compares values and returns an error on mismatch. expectError(expected_error, error_union) requires the exact error. A successful parse is unwrapped with try inside the test so the value can be compared.

sections.title: A test must be able to fail
sections.body: An empty test block passes, and a catch that ignores the error passes whether the parser works or not. Make each test assert a specific outcome. Boundary inputs such as zero, 65535, 65536, and malformed text are more valuable than several copies of the happy path.

vocabulary.definition: A named test compiled and run by the Zig test runner.
A standard assertion that returns an error when two values differ.
A standard assertion that requires a specific error from an error union.
A test at the edge of an accepted range, such as zero or the maximum.

steps.title: Test the valid value and zero boundary
steps.prompt: Edit main.zig. Fill both test blocks: one compares 8080 with a successful parse, and one expects OutOfRange for zero.
hints: The valid test needs expectEqual and a try around parsePort.
Cast 8080 to u16 so the expected type is explicit.

localVerification.description: Compiles and runs the test blocks in main.zig with the Zig test runner.

tests.description: The parser keeps the error union signature.
The valid-port test compares the parsed value.
The boundary test expects the exact error.

steps.title: The test that cannot fail
steps.prompt: A boundary test passes even when the parser returns a value for zero. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.
hints: The test catches the error and does nothing with it.
If parsing succeeds, the test also reaches the end.
The expected error must be asserted explicitly.

fixes.label: Assert that the result is true.

steps.explanation: The empty catch discards the error, and a success path simply falls off the end. expectError fails the test unless the parser returns exactly OutOfRange.

steps.title: How a failed expectation behaves
steps.prompt: A test runs `try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u16, 8080), try parsePort("8081"))`. What happens on the mismatch?
hints: The test body uses try, so that error leaves the block.
The test runner treats the error as a failure.

quiz.prompt: A test runs `try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u16, 8080), try parsePort("8081"))`. What happens on the mismatch?

options.label: expectEqual returns an error, and the test is marked failed.
It prints a message and the test still passes.
It always panics the entire process.
It skips the remaining tests in the file.

quiz.explanation: std.testing assertions return errors. The try propagates that error out of the test block, and the test runner reports a failure.
